met_analysis:
The Low Pressure area over Western parts of Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining north Jharkhand has become less marked at 0830 hrs IST of today, 18th July, 2026. However, the associated cyclonic circulation persisted over the same region and extends upto 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Amritsar, Karnal, Hardoi, Ranchi, Digha and thence southeastwards towards Northwest Bay of Bengal and extends upto 0.9 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhoodupto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over east Uttar Pradesh between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
A trough runs from North Bihar to Northwest Bay of Bengal across Jharkhand and Gangetic west Bengal between 1.5 & 3.1 Km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Southwest Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over South Odisha & neighbourhood at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood persists and now seen at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Gulf of Mannar adjoining south Tamil Nadu persists and seen between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Kerala & neighbourhood persists and now seen between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in upper level westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The trough from North Lakshadweep area to southwest Bay of Bengal across north Kerala, South Interior Karnataka and north Tamilnadu at 7.6 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
